newsitem.title: USA: Hubble service crew packs up for ride home.
newsitem.headline: Hubble service crew packs up for ride home.

text.p: NASA's Hubble tune-up crew hung up their spacesuits on Thursday and prepared for a rare nighttime landing at Florida's Kennedy Space Centre.
The seven-man crew, who successfully refurbished the Hubble Space Telescope during five outings into space, packed away their spacewalking gear and checked out shuttle Discovery's landing systems.

Forecasters were predicting generally favourable weather for the shuttle's planned touchdown at 1:49 a.m. EST (0649 GMT) on Friday. The only concern was for the chance of showers within 35 miles (56 km) of the runway.
"The weather for the Cape tomorrow is looking fairly good," mission control's Kevin Kregel informed the shuttle crew. "We think we have a good chance of getting into Kennedy."

The conditions at the Florida spaceport were forecast to deteriorate on Saturday. NASA dispatched recovery crews to the shuttle's back-up landing strip in California, where the weather was expected to be fine on Friday.
In preparation for Friday's homecoming, mission commander Ken Bowersox and copilot Scott Horowitz test-fired Discovery's manoeuvring jets and powered up the hydraulic system.
Discovery's landing would be only the ninth in the history of the shuttle programme to take place in darkness.

Bowersox's landing will be aided by the recent installation of 52 Halogen lights down the centre of the shuttle's 15,000 -foot (4,572 m) -long runway. Shuttle commanders requested the modification to help them keep the gliding shuttle lined up for a perfect touchdown.
NASA officials said they expected nighttime and low-light dawn landings to become more commonplace.

Discovery blasted off from the Kennedy Space Centre before dawn on Feb. 11. The astronauts captured the Hubble Space Telescope two days later and made $350 million worth of upgrades before releasing it again early on Wednesday.
